title: The missed middle case
idea: A chain that handles 'high' and 'low' but forgets the value in between — a whole case is never covered.

exercises.prompt: Rule: hot if temp > 25, cold if temp < 10. The code only has those two ifs. What about temp = 18?
options: Nothing prints — the middle case is missed
exercises.explanation: 18 is neither > 25 nor < 10, so neither branch runs — a whole middle range was forgotten.

options: The in-between range has no branch
exercises.explanation: The chain covers the extremes but not the values between them. A 'mild' case is missing.

exercises.prompt: Which value proves the middle case is missing?
exercises.explanation: A value like 18 sits between the two limits and falls through. Testing a middle value exposes the gap.

exercises.prompt: Plan a chain that covers ALL temperatures (high, low, and the rest).
exercises.explanation: Test hot, then cold, then let else catch every remaining (mild) value so nothing falls through.

exercises.prompt: Adding an else branch guarantees every input is handled.
exercises.explanation: True. else has no condition, so any input that missed every if/elif lands there — no gaps left.

exercises.prompt: After adding 'else -> Mild', temp = 18 prints what?
exercises.explanation: 18 misses hot and cold, so the else runs: 'Mild'. The gap is closed.

exercises.prompt: A grade chain has 'A' for 90+ and 'C' for under 70, nothing else. A score of 80 gives…
exercises.explanation: 80 is below 90 and not under 70, so no branch matches — the B range (70-89) was forgotten.

exercises.prompt: Best way to catch a missed case BEFORE running the code?
options: Hand-trace a value from every range, including the middle
exercises.explanation: List a few representative inputs across the whole range and hand-check each finds a branch.

exercises.prompt: Why is 'nothing prints' a dangerous bug?
options: It is silent, so the gap is easy to miss
exercises.explanation: Silent output looks like nothing is wrong, so the missed case can slip through unnoticed.

exercises.prompt: Covering extremes is not the same as covering every case.
exercises.explanation: Right. High and low are only two cases; the values between them need a branch too (often an else).
